name: The Westin Miyako Kyoto
positioning: The Westin Miyako Kyoto: a hotel opened in 1890 at the edge of the Higashiyama mountains in eastern Kyoto, with natural hot spring baths and a Togo Murano-designed annex
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to eastern Kyoto's temples and shrines
Guests who want onsen bathing during a city stay

facts.text: The hotel opened in 1890 at the base of Higashiyama.
Nearby temples and shrines include the Heian Shrine, Nanzenji, Eikando and Ginkakuji.
Spa KACHO's design was inspired by the brick, moss-covered Suirokaku aqueduct at Nanzenji Temple.
Le Jardin Sothys offers programs including hot spring baths, traditional Japanese massage, acupressure, moxibustion and meditation.
The hotel arranges experiences such as hotel tours, sake tasting and kimono fittings.
The Westin Club lounge serves coffee, tea and other drinks, with a cocktail hour at the end of the day.
RAQOU, the all-day restaurant, overlooks Higashiyama and the city of Kyoto.
The hotel has a satellite concierge baggage counter at Kyoto Station for guests.

highlights.text: Kyoto Keage Onsen hot spring water flows from the ground beneath the hotel, feeding indoor and semi-open-air onsen baths for men and women.
The Kasui-en annex was designed by architect Togo Murano in 1959 and is hailed as a masterpiece of modernist Japanese architecture.
The hotel is in eastern Kyoto at the edge of the Higashiyama mountain range, with numerous UNESCO heritage sites within walking distance.
Spa KACHO's semi-open-air bath looks out on the hotel's garden leading to Mount Kacho.
Rooms use soft curving forms and wood floors and walls, with carpets inspired by Kyoto's kawadoko river-floor summer dining.

considerations.text: The closest airport is Osaka International Airport (Itami), about 60 kilometers away.
